title: People’s Mañanera October 16
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Returning What Was Stolen to the People: From Corruption to Well-Being  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that the mansion of drug kingpin
Negro Durazo will be converted into a university and a high school, with an
investment of more than 150 million pesos (US$8.33 million). In addition, 800
million pesos (US$44.45 million) will be allocated to the Pension Fund for
Well-Being, and 200 million pesos (US$11.11 million) recovered from the case
of former Security Minister García Luna, currently imprisoned in the United
States, will go to schools in Guerrero.

**More Public Education for Youth  
** Rosario Castellanos University will open 28 new campuses in 20 states and
10 more in the eastern part of Mexico City. Sheinbaum announced an arts high
school for 1,200 young students in Tlalpan, as part of the goal to create
400,000 new educational spaces during her six-year term in office.

**Security: Homicides and High-Impact Crimes Decline  
** Sheinbaum noted that under former president Felipe Calderón, the average
daily number of homicides rose from 24 to 74, and under Enrique Peña, they
reached 100. In contrast, under the Fourth Transformation (4T), they fell to
47.1; high-impact crimes have declined by 36%, and the perception of public
insecurity decreased to 35.9%.

**Mexico Strengthens Its Exports Despite Tariffs  
** Sheinbaum highlighted the Economic Commission on Latin America and the
Caribbean (ECLAC)’s projections on the growth of Mexican exports, driven by
the electronics and automotive industries, as well as by the opening of new
markets in Europe and Japan.
